title: Tie Rod Replacement
summary: Steering blueprint for confirming inner or outer tie rod wear, steering looseness, and alignment needs before quoting replacement.
symptoms: Loose steering, wander, or delayed steering response
Clunk or knock from the steering linkage
Uneven front tire wear, feathering, or toe-related wear
Steering wheel off-center after impact or suspension work
inspect_first: Outer tie rod end play at the wheel and at the joint
Inner tie rod play under the rack boot and steering rack condition
Rack boot tears, grease loss, corrosion, and jam nut condition
Ball joints, control arms, wheel bearings, and tire condition before blaming steering linkage
likely_causes: Impact damage or seized adjustment hardware
repair_overview: Identify whether the failed part is the inner tie rod, outer tie rod end, or both.
Mark or measure the tie rod position to keep the vehicle close enough for alignment travel.
Remove the cotter pin, nut, jam nut, boot, or inner joint hardware as required.
Install the replacement part, torque fasteners, and secure boots or cotter pins.
Set toe close enough for a safe alignment trip, then perform or recommend alignment.
common_mistakes: Replacing an outer tie rod when the inner joint has the actual play
Skipping inspection of rack boots and steering rack leakage
Failing to recommend alignment after changing toe hardware
Overlooking seized jam nuts that change labor time
estimate_guidance: Specify inner, outer, left, right, or paired service so the estimate matches the repair.
Include wheel alignment as a normal follow-up after tie rod replacement.
Flag seized jam nuts, torn rack boots, and steering rack leakage before final approval.
Do not bundle ball joints or control arms unless the inspection proves additional play.

recommended_repairs.title: Wheel Alignment
recommended_repairs.description: Tie rod replacement changes toe, so alignment should be planned with the repair.

recommended_repairs.title: Steering Pull Diagnosis
recommended_repairs.description: Use when the complaint includes pull, off-center steering, or tire wear without confirmed tie rod play.

recommended_repairs.title: Suspension Noise Diagnosis
recommended_repairs.description: Use when looseness may involve ball joints, control arms, links, or wheel bearings.

diagnostic_context.intro: Tie rod estimates are strongest when the inspection separates inner joint wear from outer end play and includes alignment planning.
